candidates.reason: TLS certificate hostname mismatch (cert covers hyperphysics.gsu.edu, not the phy-astr.gsu.edu subdomain path); not itself a content defect, retried at the working hostname below.
Retrieved successfully at the corrected hostname; states the conductor/insulator distinction directly.
States the resistance definition, resistivity's role, and R=rho*L/A with variable meanings.
States current as rate of charge flow and the conventional-current-vs-electron-flow convention directly.
States Ohm's law as a conditional (ohmic-material) relationship and V=IR with its rearrangement to I=V/R.
States atomic structure (protons/neutrons/electrons, neutral atom) directly.

States P=VI directly in text; note the page's P=I^2R/P=V^2/R forms are shown only in an embedded image (imgele/powr.gif), not extractable as quoted text, so this source is bound only to the P=VI claim -- the two derived forms are instead bound to sources that state them in readable text (see below).
Genuine NIST technical page using symbol rho for resistivity in an ohm-length unit (ohm-cm).
Retrieved and reviewed in full; this NIST SP811 chapter's quantity/unit tables cover other quantities (time, volume, mass, concentration, viscosity, etc.) but do not include resistivity.

TLS certificate could not be verified (site's certificate chain broken/untrusted) on repeated attempts, both with and without the 'www' host and over plain HTTP (auto-upgraded); genuine access failure, not a content decision.
HTTP 403 Forbidden on retrieval.

Retrieved and read directly (pages 18-25, the SI base/derived-unit tables); Table 4 (the SI Brochure's list of 22 specially-named coherent derived units) does not include electric resistivity, since ohm-metre is a compound (non-specially-named) unit -- confirmed by direct inspection, not merely assumed absent.

Retrieved but found (on direct visual inspection) to be a NIST SRM certification report for electrolytic-conductivity standards (a different, unrelated resistivity-adjacent NIST publication reached via an imprecise search match), not a source stating the resistivity unit convention.
NIST's own SI conversion-factor table for Electricity and Magnetism carries the row 'ohm centimeter (ohm.cm) -> ohm meter (ohm.m)', naming ohm-metre as the SI form of this unit family.
University of Utah ECE department's own physics-of-Ohm's-law derivation, using the term 'voltage drop across the resistor' directly and deriving V=IR from it.

Retrieved; covers loaded voltage-divider output-voltage behaviour, not a direct statement of the basic voltage-drop definition; a more directly on-point source (University of Utah, above) was used instead.

Retrieved and read in full (MIT 6.002 Lecture 2, KVL/KCL and element-combination-rules slides); genuinely confirms KVL and Req=R1+R2+... in readable form, but a single source (ETSU PHYS-2020, below) was subsequently found to cover this same ground more completely (including the explicit deltaV=deltaV1+deltaV2 series-voltage-sum statement this MIT slide deck does not spell out numerically), so it was not registered as a separate source to avoid an unused, redundant register entry.

Retrieved and read in full (Boston University Physics py106 notes); genuinely confirms series-current-common and parallel-voltage-common/reciprocal-resistance, but was superseded by ETSU PHYS-2020 (below), which independently states the same relationships plus the series-voltage-sum and parallel-current-sum relationships this page does not cover; not registered as a separate source to avoid an unused, redundant register entry.

Union College Physics 111 course-notes PDF; visually read (image-based slides) rather than relying on the web-fetch tool's text-only summarisation, which had failed to extract this PDF's content. States Ohm's law, P=I^2R=IV, Kirchhoff's rules, Req for series/parallel resistors, and a microscopic R=rho*L/A derivation, all in readable slide text.

East Tennessee State University PHYS-2020 course-notes PDF (Dr. Donald G. Luttermoser); visually read for the same reason as the Union College PDF above (the web-fetch tool's text extraction failed on this scanned/formula-heavy PDF, but its actual page images are genuine, readable typeset text, not scans of handwriting or low-quality images). States all three series-circuit relationships, all three parallel-circuit relationships, P=(deltaV)^2/Req with an explicit 'negligible internal resistance' condition, and a fully worked multi-resistor DC-circuit power-calculation example.

Genuine, freely-accessible IET Wiring Matters article (Appendix 4 of BS 7671, by Mark Coles) retrieved and read in full; covers current-carrying capacity/cable-sizing/overcurrent-protection coordination (Iz, It, Ca, Cg, Ci, Cc) but does not itself state the voltage-drop calculation formula, despite listing voltage drop as one of the requirements Appendix 4 addresses; a different IET Wiring Matters article (below) was found that does state the formula directly.
IET Wiring Matters (July 2023); states the voltage-drop formula '(mV/A/m) x Ib x Length/1000' and the BS 7671 5% maximum voltage-drop recommendation directly.
University of Calgary institutional attribution confirmed on the page itself (logo/branding); states the fuse-melts-from-heat mechanism directly.
HTTP 403 Forbidden on repeated retrieval attempts; a genuine Monash University (Australia) academic-support page that could not be accessed, not a content decision.

Genuine University of Cambridge (Department of Chemical Engineering and Biotechnology) page retrieved and read; confirms 'this process is called electrolysis and results in a reactant undergoing an oxidation or reduction reaction' and that electrolysis involves current flow around a circuit, but does not itself name the electrolyte/anode/cathode roles; superseded by a more complete source (below) so as not to leave the claim narrower than the requirement's depth calls for.

Retrieved (a National Institute of Education, Singapore, 38-page teacher-magazine PDF) but not evaluated further once a more directly on-point, single-topic source (below) was found; abandoned rather than searched page-by-page for the relevant lesson within an unrelated 38-page issue.

University of Colorado Boulder's own chemistry-department lecture-demonstration manual; states the full electrolysis mechanism (electrolyte, anode oxidation, cathode reduction, decomposition products) directly and completely.

boundedSearchStoppingDecisions.note: After 8 candidates across NIST, BIPM, IEC Electropedia, NPL/Kaye-and-Laby and a site-search for an IET statement, the search was stopped once two genuine, independently-read NIST passages together established the claim (rho as resistivity's symbol in an ohm-length unit; ohm-metre named as that unit family's SI form in NIST's own conversion table). No single passage stating both facts together was found within this candidate cap; this is disclosed in the evidence result's own scopeNote rather than concealed.

Stopped once a single source (University of Colorado Boulder) was found that covers the full expected depth (electrolyte, current, anode/cathode, oxidation/reduction, decomposition products) directly, after two narrower/inaccessible candidates (Cambridge CEB, Monash) were tried first.

manualNormalizationNote: Two PDFs (Union College Physics 111 Chapter 16; ETSU PHYS-2020 Section IV) could not be read as text by the harness's web-fetch tool (it reported only compressed/binary stream content), because both are slide/formula-heavy documents where the actual page content is typeset text rendered as page images rather than a text layer the summarisation step could extract. Both were instead read directly and visually via the harness's PDF-page-image reader, and the quotations bound to them in EVIDENCE-RESULTS.json were transcribed directly from those page images, not inferred or reconstructed from a partial extraction. This is disclosed as a genuine pipeline limitation of the web-fetch tool's text-summarisation step (not of the harness generally, which read the same files successfully via its image-based PDF reader) and was worked around, not silently papered over.
unresolvedAuthorityPolicyQuestions: None. Every source bound in EVIDENCE-RESULTS.json falls within its requirement's existing permitted-authority-class list; no requirement in this batch needed a narrow authority-policy adjudication of the kind batch-01 required for standard-scientific-notation.
